advisories.title: SQL injection via metadata filter key in SQLite checkpointer
advisories.detail: User-controlled filter keys are interpolated into checkpoint queries without parameterization, enabling SQL injection that can chain to RCE via forged checkpoint rows.

advisories.title: Unsafe msgpack deserialization in checkpoint loading
advisories.detail: LangGraph checkpoint loading deserializes msgpack payloads unsafely; a crafted checkpoint can execute code during load.

advisories.title: Unsafe JSON deserialization in checkpoint loading
advisories.detail: Checkpoint loading deserializes JSON payloads without type restrictions, allowing untrusted-data deserialization.

advisories.title: Path traversal in legacy load_prompt functions
advisories.detail: Legacy prompt-loading APIs resolve user-supplied paths without containment, permitting arbitrary file read via path traversal. See also LD304 (load_prompt usage).

advisories.title: Serialization-injection secret extraction in dumps/loads
advisories.detail: Crafted serialized payloads inject attributes during load, enabling extraction of secrets embedded in serialized objects. Fixed on both the 0.3.x and 1.x lines. (CNA scores 9.3; NVD scores 8.2.)

advisories.title: Unauthenticated RCE in /api/v1/validate/code
advisories.detail: Missing authentication on the code-validation endpoint lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary code via crafted HTTP requests (Python decorator / default-argument abuse). Exploited in the wild to deploy the Flodrix botnet; added to CISA KEV on 2025-05-05.

advisories.title: BaseCache deserialization of untrusted data may lead to RCE
advisories.detail: The BaseCache implementation deserializes untrusted cached data, which can lead to remote code execution.

advisories.title: RCE in "json" mode of JsonPlusSerializer
advisories.detail: The JsonPlusSerializer in "json" mode reconstructs arbitrary objects during deserialization, enabling remote code execution.

advisories.title: SQL injection in the SQLite store implementation
advisories.detail: The SQLite store implementation is vulnerable to SQL injection. Distinct from LD101 (fixed 3.0.1): a project pinned between 2.0.11 and 3.0.1 is safe from this one but still exposed to LD101. Affects 2.0.8 and later only: the SQLite store first shipped in 2.0.8 — the 2.0.5–2.0.7 wheels and source trees contain no langgraph/store/sqlite — so earlier releases have no such code, although GHSA and OSV give the range as starting at 0.

advisories.title: SQL injection via filter key in SqliteStore
advisories.detail: Filter keys passed to SqliteStore are interpolated into queries unsafely, enabling SQL injection (public PoC). Affects 2.0.8 and later only: the SQLite store first shipped in 2.0.8 — the 2.0.5–2.0.7 wheels and source trees contain no langgraph/store/sqlite — so earlier releases have no such code, although GHSA and OSV give the range as starting at 0.

advisories.title: Path traversal to RCE via /api/v2/files upload
advisories.detail: upload_user_file() does not sanitize the multipart filename, allowing path traversal to write arbitrary files (escalating to RCE via cron/config overwrite). Unauthenticated when auto-login is enabled (see LD403). Actively exploited (VulnCheck). Also fixed in langflow-base 0.8.3. NOT yet indexed by OSV at build time; likely the same root cause as OSV's CVE-2026-33309 (arbitrary file write via v2 API, fixed 1.9.0) — recorded as a hypothesis, not hard-merged.

advisories.title: Unsafe URL path construction in LangGraph SDK
advisories.detail: DEPRECATED 2026-11-19 — superseded by LD133; this ID no longer produces findings. It followed PYSEC-2026-2194, which files CVE-2026-48776 under the langgraph package although its own text, the vendor advisory GHSA-w39p-vh2g-g8g5 and the fix release (sdk==0.3.15) all name langgraph-sdk. It therefore compared langgraph versions against an SDK fix number and missed the installs that matter: langgraph 0.3.34 pins langgraph-sdk < 0.2.0 and 0.6.11 pins < 0.3.0, so both always resolve a vulnerable SDK, yet neither was flagged. LD133 checks langgraph-sdk itself. Original summary: the LangGraph SDK builds request URLs from unsanitized path segments, letting a caller-controlled value alter the request target (fixed in langgraph-sdk 0.3.15). CNA (GitHub) scores this 4.2 medium; an NVD secondary analyst assigns a maximal-impact 9.1 vector inconsistent with the SDK URL-construction root cause.

advisories.title: Template injection via attribute access in prompt templates
advisories.detail: Prompt templates evaluate attribute access on template variables, so a crafted template string can traverse object attributes to read sensitive values (e.g. secrets reachable from a passed object). Fixed on both the 0.3.x and 1.x lines. Scored with CVSS 4.0 (base 8.3).

advisories.title: Path traversal and sandbox escape in file-search middleware and loaders
advisories.detail: The file-search agent middleware and the prompt and chain/agent configuration loaders resolve user-influenced paths without containment, permitting path traversal and sandbox escape to read files outside the intended root. Local vector, high attack complexity, confidentiality impact. The 1.3.9 fix is to the middleware, which exists only on the 1.x line; the configuration loaders the advisory also names ship in the 0.x wheels (langchain/chains/loading.py), which is why 0.x pins are in range although the only patched version is 1.3.9. The same advisory covers path-prefix checks in langchain-anthropic (fixed in 1.4.6): see LD135.

advisories.title: SSRF via image_url token counting in get_num_tokens_from_messages
advisories.detail: DEPRECATED 2026-11-19 — superseded by LD134; this ID no longer produces findings. It followed the package metadata of GHSA-2g6r-c272-w58r and PYSEC-2026-2562 (langchain-core < 1.2.11), but the advisory's own text places the vulnerable code in langchain_openai/chat_models/base.py and says it is patched in langchain-openai 1.1.9, which requires langchain-core 1.2.11; the fix commit adds only an SSRF-validation helper to langchain-core. Matching langchain-core therefore flagged projects that do not install langchain-openai at all, and missed projects that upgraded langchain-core but kept langchain-openai below 1.1.9 (1.1.8 accepts any core from 1.2.9). LD134 checks langchain-openai itself. Original summary: ChatOpenAI.get_num_tokens_from_messages fetches image_url contents while counting tokens, so a crafted message URL can drive server-side requests to attacker-chosen hosts.

advisories.title: Incomplete f-string validation in prompt templates
advisories.detail: f-string prompt-template validation is incomplete, letting crafted template input reach unintended evaluation paths (information disclosure). Same family as LD113. Fixed on both the 0.3.x and 1.x lines.

advisories.title: Unsafe deserialization via overly broad load() allowlists
advisories.detail: langchain-core's load()/loads() allowlists are too broad, so a crafted serialized payload can reconstruct attacker-controlled objects during deserialization (high-confidentiality impact, can chain further). Fixed on both the 0.3.x and 1.x lines.

advisories.title: Namespace prefix matching crosses segment boundaries in the SQLite store
advisories.detail: Hierarchical namespaces are flattened to a dot-joined string and scoped reads match it with LIKE '<path>%'. Because LIKE ignores the '.' separator, a scoped search or list_namespaces also returns sibling namespaces sharing leading characters (e.g. namespace ('memories','alice') also matches 'alice_admin'), leaking cross-tenant state. Same CVE as LD119, which covers the Postgres store. Affects 2.0.8 and later only: the SQLite store first shipped in 2.0.8 — the 2.0.5–2.0.7 wheels and source trees contain no langgraph/store/sqlite — so earlier releases have no such code, although GHSA and OSV give the range as starting at 0.

advisories.title: Namespace prefix matching crosses segment boundaries in the Postgres store
advisories.detail: Same root cause as LD118 (one CVE, two packages): namespaces are stored dot-joined and scoped reads use LIKE '<path>%', so a scoped search or list_namespaces also returns sibling namespaces sharing leading characters, leaking cross-tenant state. Tracked separately so the fix line names the package actually installed.

advisories.title: CORS misconfiguration to token hijack, account takeover and RCE
advisories.detail: allow_origins='*' combined with allow_credentials=True and a refresh-token cookie set to SameSite=None lets any attacker-controlled page call the refresh endpoint with the victim's credentials and obtain fresh access/refresh token pairs. The stolen session reaches authenticated endpoints, chaining to remote code execution. Added to CISA KEV on 2026-05-21. Score is the NVD primary CVSS 3.1 base (8.8); the VulnCheck CNA rates it 9.4 critical on CVSS 4.0.

advisories.title: Unauthenticated RCE via the exec_globals parameter of the validate endpoint
advisories.detail: The validate endpoint accepts an attacker-supplied exec_globals mapping and includes it in the execution context, so a remote unauthenticated caller executes arbitrary code — in the default container, as root. Reported through ZDI (ZDI-26-036); added to CISA KEV on 2026-07-21. OSV records no fixed version for this advisory: the 1.8.0 bound comes from the NVD CPE range (affected up to and including 1.7.3) plus the absence of any 1.7.4 release, making 1.8.0 the first unaffected release.

advisories.title: Unauthenticated RCE via attacker-supplied flow data in build_public_tmp
advisories.detail: POST /api/v1/build_public_tmp/{flow_id}/flow builds public flows without authentication, and when the optional data parameter is supplied it uses attacker-controlled node definitions instead of the stored flow, passing that Python code to exec() with no sandboxing. Distinct from CVE-2025-3248 (LD106), which fixed /api/v1/validate/code. Added to CISA KEV on 2026-03-25. Sources disagree on the bound: the vendor GHSA and OSV say fixed in 1.9.0 while the NVD CPE stops at 1.8.2 — we take the wider vendor bound so a 1.8.2-1.8.4 install is still flagged.

advisories.title: IDOR in /api/v1/responses runs another user's flow
advisories.detail: The /api/v1/responses endpoint does not check flow ownership, so any authenticated user can execute an arbitrary flow belonging to another tenant by passing the victim's flow ID — reaching that flow's credentials, tools and data. Added to CISA KEV on 2026-07-07: a lower-CVSS authorization bug that is trivially exploitable in practice. GHSA and NVD both fix it at 1.9.1; PYSEC-2026-221 records 1.9.2, and we take the vendor value.

advisories.title: auto_login to validate/code chain gives unauthenticated RCE
advisories.detail: /api/v1/auto_login mints SUPERUSER tokens to any caller that can reach the port, and /api/v1/validate/code executes submitted code via exec(). Chaining the two is full remote code execution against a default deployment in two HTTP requests. Added to CISA KEV on 2026-08-04 with a three-day remediation deadline. Not indexed by OSV as of 2026-08-27 — surfaced via NVD plus the CISA KEV catalog, so the weekly OSV watcher could not have seen it. See also LD403, which flags the auto-login configuration itself.

advisories.title: SSRF via unrestricted requests in the OpenAPI RequestsToolkit
advisories.detail: langchain_community.agent_toolkits.openapi.toolkit.RequestsToolkit places no restriction on the addresses it will fetch, so an agent steered by untrusted input can reach localhost and internal network services — cloud instance metadata, admin endpoints, internal APIs — from the application's own network position. Fixed in 0.0.28. Note the unusual timeline: the fix shipped in March 2024 but the CVE was only published on 2025-06-23, so any currently maintained install is already well past the boundary; this entry exists for completeness and for projects pinned to a pre-0.0.28 line. NVD's primary analyst score is 10.0 (PR:N/UI:N, scope changed); the huntr CNA scores the same issue 8.4 (PR:H/UI:R).

advisories.title: XXE in EverNoteLoader via unguarded iterparse()
advisories.detail: EverNoteLoader parses .enex exports with etree.iterparse() without disabling external entity resolution, so a crafted note export can read local files or force outbound requests when it is ingested. Fixed in 0.3.27. Sources disagree on the affected version: the huntr write-up (mirrored by NVD) names 0.3.63, but langchain-community has no such release — its 0.3 line stops at 0.3.31 — so that number is the reporter's langchain-core version, not this package's. GHSA and OSV agree on < 0.3.27, which is what the range above compares against. NVD carries no primary score (status Deferred); 7.5 is the huntr CNA base score.

advisories.title: SSRF via nested sitemap entries in SitemapLoader
advisories.detail: SitemapLoader.parse_sitemap enforces the documented restrict_to_same_domain control only on leaf <url> entries. The loop over nested <sitemap> index entries passes each child <loc> straight to scrape_all(), so a sitemap index pointing at an internal address is fetched despite the restriction. NO RELEASED FIX: upstream closed the issue on 2026-08-13, but no langchain-community release carries it — 0.4.2 (2026-05-22) is still the newest, which is why this advisory has no fix version and langdoctor prints no upgrade line. Mitigate by not pointing SitemapLoader at untrusted sitemaps and by restricting egress from the ingestion host. VulnCheck scores it 8.6 on CVSS 3.1 and 7.7 on CVSS 4.0; NVD has no primary score yet (status Received).

advisories.title: Namespace labels containing '.' reach other namespaces (SQLite store)
advisories.detail: The SQLite store saves a namespace as its labels joined with '.', so ('tenant', 'bob') and ('tenant.bob',) are the same stored namespace. put() rejected labels containing '.', but get, search, delete, list_namespaces, their async variants and ops passed straight to batch/abatch did not — a caller who controls a namespace label can read, overwrite or delete another tenant's items. Follow-up to CVE-2026-71433 (LD118): 3.1.1 fixed that one but is still affected here. Fixed in 3.1.2, which requires langgraph-checkpoint 4.3.0. Same CVE as LD129 (Postgres store, fixed in 3.1.3). NVD has no primary score yet (status Awaiting Analysis); 6.0 is the GitHub CNA CVSS 4.0 base score. Affects 2.0.8 and later only: the SQLite store first shipped in 2.0.8 — the 2.0.5–2.0.7 wheels and source trees contain no langgraph/store/sqlite — so earlier releases have no such code, although GHSA and OSV give the range as starting at 0.

advisories.title: Namespace labels containing '.' reach other namespaces (Postgres store)
advisories.detail: Same root cause as LD128 (one CVE, two packages): PostgresStore and AsyncPostgresStore flatten a namespace with '.'.join(), and only put() rejected labels containing '.', so get, search, delete, list_namespaces and batch/abatch ops can read, overwrite or delete items in another tenant's namespace. Unlike LD118/LD119 the two stores were fixed in different releases — Postgres in 3.1.3 (which requires langgraph-checkpoint 4.3.0) — so this is tracked separately and the fix line names the right version. NVD has no primary score yet; 6.0 is the GitHub CNA CVSS 4.0 base score.

advisories.title: Unencoded thread/assistant ids in SDK v3 streaming redirect GETs
advisories.detail: The v3 streaming client interpolates caller-supplied thread_id and assistant_id into request paths without _quote_path_param (get_tree and _fetch_state, sync and async). Relative path segments then redirect an authenticated GET to another path on the configured server — through thread_id the attacker also controls the query string (e.g. /store/items?namespace=...&key=...). Read-only: no write primitive. Only applications that pass attacker-controlled text as a streaming thread_id or assistant_id are affected. The v3 stream module does not exist on the 0.3.x line, so only 0.4.0–0.4.5 are affected; fixed in 0.4.6. Same CVE as LD131 (RemoteGraph in langgraph). NVD has no primary score yet; 4.3 is the GitHub CNA CVSS 3.1 base score.

advisories.title: RemoteGraph v3 streaming passes unencoded thread ids to the SDK
advisories.detail: From langgraph 1.2.3, RemoteGraph v3 streaming passes config['configurable']['thread_id'] into threads.stream(...), and its dependency range admits the vulnerable langgraph-sdk 0.4.0–0.4.5 (LD130), whose unencoded path parameters let a crafted thread_id redirect an authenticated GET to another path on the server. Fixed in 1.2.14, which requires langgraph-sdk >= 0.4.6. Exploitable only when the installed langgraph-sdk is also affected and an attacker controls the thread_id; a project that already pins langgraph-sdk >= 0.4.6 is not exposed through this path. NVD has no primary score yet; 4.3 is the GitHub CNA CVSS 3.1 base score.

advisories.title: Custom-auth decorators ignore actions= and skip fallback handlers
advisories.detail: The resource-scoped authorization decorators @auth.on.threads, @auth.on.assistants and @auth.on.crons ignore their actions= argument: a handler meant for, say, actions=['create'] is registered for every action on the resource. Because that resource-wide handler is selected before broader fallback handlers, authorization checks living in those fallbacks never run, and an authenticated user may read, update or delete another user's threads, assistants or crons. Only Python deployments that use actions= on these decorators are affected; a handler that itself enforces action, ownership and permission checks for every request stays safe. No workaround — upgrade to 0.4.4. NVD has no primary score yet (status Awaiting Analysis); 7.6 is the GitHub CNA CVSS 4.0 base score.

advisories.title: Unsafe URL path construction in the LangGraph SDK (langgraph-sdk)
advisories.detail: The LangGraph SDK builds request URLs from unsanitized path segments, letting a caller-controlled value alter the request target. Fixed in langgraph-sdk 0.3.15. Same CVE as LD112: the vendor advisory (GHSA-w39p-vh2g-g8g5) and PYSEC-2026-2575 attribute it to langgraph-sdk, while PYSEC-2026-2194 — which LD112 followed — files it under the langgraph package. LD112 is deprecated in favor of this entry, which checks the package the vendor actually names, so an old SDK is flagged whichever langgraph sits next to it. CNA (GitHub) scores this 4.2 medium; the NVD-secondary 9.1 is inconsistent with the root cause, as noted on LD112.

advisories.title: SSRF via image_url token counting in ChatOpenAI (langchain-openai)
advisories.detail: ChatOpenAI.get_num_tokens_from_messages fetches image_url contents while counting tokens, so a crafted message URL can drive server-side requests to attacker-chosen hosts. Low severity (availability-only impact, high attack complexity). The vulnerable code is langchain_openai/chat_models/base.py; the vendor advisory says it is patched in langchain-openai 1.1.9, which requires langchain-core 1.2.11 for the new SSRF check. Upgrading langchain-core alone changes nothing, because langchain-openai 1.1.8 accepts it too. Same CVE as LD115, which followed the GHSA/PYSEC package attribution to langchain-core. Verified 2026-11-19 against the advisory text, the fix commit and the PyPI metadata of langchain-openai 1.1.8 and 1.1.9. The check added in 1.1.9 could itself be bypassed until 1.1.14: see LD136.

advisories.title: Path-prefix authorization bypass in the Anthropic tools middleware (langchain-anthropic)
advisories.detail: The Anthropic tools middleware checks a requested path against its allowed prefixes as plain strings, without a path-segment boundary, so a sibling path that merely shares the prefix is accepted and access reaches beyond the intended subtree. Same advisory and CVE as LD114, which covers the langchain package; tracked separately so the fix line names the package actually installed. The module it concerns (langchain_anthropic/middleware/anthropic_tools.py) first ships in 1.0.0 — the 0.3.22 wheel has no middleware — so earlier releases are out of range although GHSA gives '<= 1.4.5'. Verified 2026-11-20 against the advisory text, the fix commit and the PyPI wheels.

advisories.title: Image-URL SSRF check bypassable by DNS rebinding (langchain-openai)
advisories.detail: The SSRF check that langchain-openai 1.1.9 added to image token counting (the fix for LD134) validated a URL and then fetched it in a separate network operation with its own DNS resolution. An attacker-controlled hostname could resolve to a public address for the check and to a private or localhost address for the fetch. Impact is limited to blind probing: the response is only handed to an image parser and never returned. Fixed in 1.1.14 with a transport that resolves once and pins the connection (requires langchain-core 1.2.31). CVSS 3.1 from the CNA, as recorded by NVD. Verified 2026-11-20 against GHSA, NVD and OSV.

advisories.title: Langflow older than the current secure baseline (1.13.0)
advisories.detail: Langflow has a large and fast-moving CVE history. Versions below 1.13.0 carry multiple known vulnerabilities beyond those enumerated individually here. The baseline moved from 1.11.0 to 1.13.0 because IBM PSIRT published about 99 further Langflow CVEs between 2026-08-28 and 2026-11-08 with fixes ranging from 1.11.2 to 1.13.0 — 16 of them CVSS 9.0 or higher, including CVE-2026-110186 (remote code execution through 1.12.8, CVSS 9.8); OSV had indexed none of them as of 2026-11-18. The 1.12.9 and 1.12.10 maintenance releases shipped after 1.13.0, but they branch from release-1.12.8 and backport only the 1.13.0 -> 1.13.1 delta (langflow PR #16119), so they stay below the baseline. Upgrade to the latest release. (Aggregate advisory: the engine suppresses this when a more specific Langflow finding already fired for the same install.)
